domain: The remaining unsolved mathematics that matters downstream, and the order AI cracks it

bottlenecks.name: Turbulence, transition and reacting-flow fidelity
bottlenecks.description: Wall heat flux, combustion stability, plume heating, reentry wakes and separation all rest on turbulence and transition closures that are calibrated, not derived. CFD Vision 2030 named turbulence, transition and separated flow as the leading gap (general). The pure-math frontier here (Navier-Stokes regularity, Onsager/anomalous dissipation, Kolmogorov scaling) is famous but far from the engineering error, which is model-form error in wall-bounded, compressible, reacting flows.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~25% of the mathematical/modeling effort behind space vehicles (judgment, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low for the famous problems (frontier-ns-unforced, frontier-turbulence-rigorous are P5 with nil engineering effect); medium for the less famous ones that actually block design: nonuniqueness maps that tell V&V where the equation is at fault (frontier-nonuniqueness-map) and derivatives of chaotic averages that would make gradient design of unsteady flows possible (frontier-chaos-linear-response). Genuinely open research; data binds once theory is cheap.

bottlenecks.name: Verification, validation and uncertainty quantification
bottlenecks.description: Solution verification (grid studies), credibility assessment under NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024), margins, rare-event probabilities (conjunction Pc, structural failure at 1e-6) and model-form error. Practice uses estimated, not guaranteed, numerical error, and Gaussian or asymptotic statistics at scale (Starlink alone performed 144,000+ collision-avoidance maneuvers in six months per 33FG, Oct 2025).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. Mostly solved in principle but expert-scarce: guaranteed a posteriori bounds, certified rare-event estimators, verified stiff integrators (frontier-certified-pde-error, frontier-rare-event-certified, frontier-stiff-certified). On-demand AI is the unlock; the residual limit is data, since no estimator beats the information content of tests.

bottlenecks.name: Optimization, control and scheduling with guarantees
bottlenecks.description: Trajectory optimization, guidance laws, reachability for collision avoidance, constellation tasking and ground-station siting, and verification of learned components. Engineers want certificates (stability, optimality gap, safety envelope) for bespoke problems, plus to know what is impossible.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. Ceilings act now (frontier-approx-ceilings, frontier-nn-verification-complexity, P3); HJB guarantees and global-optimality certificates are mostly expert-scarce rather than open (frontier-hjb-guarantees, frontier-scalable-global-certificates).

bottlenecks.name: Kinetic and plasma models (rarefied flow, electric propulsion, space weather)
bottlenecks.description: Boltzmann/DSMC for rarefied reentry and plumes, Vlasov/Landau kinetics for thrusters and the magnetosphere, MHD for space weather. Well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Boltzmann/Landau equations, general Landau damping and 3D MHD regularity are open; closures (anomalous transport) are the engineering bottleneck.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. The open well-posedness problems sit at the difficulty level that fell in Sep-Oct 2026 (362 Vlasov-Maxwell, T3), so they likely fall first (frontier-kinetic-global-regularity, frontier-landau-damping-general, frontier-mhd-wellposedness) but act through P5 (confidence). Quantitative rates and constants are the useful by-product.

bottlenecks.name: Long-term dynamics (n-body, cislunar, debris)
bottlenecks.description: Mission design runs on numerical propagation; rigorous stability and transport bounds exist only for model problems or tiny masses. Arnold diffusion was proven in the planetary 4-body problem only in 2024 (Clarke-Fejoz-Guardia).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-to-medium. Realistic-constant theorems are open and hard (frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion); finite-horizon certified transport for cislunar orbits is expert-scarce and belongs to the astrodynamics domain.

bottlenecks.name: Materials and chemistry from first principles
bottlenecks.description: DFT accuracy is limited by the unknown exchange-correlation functional; computing it exactly is QMA-hard, and learned functionals (Skala, 2.8 kcal/mol on GMTKN55, Jun 2025) are empirical. Reaction networks for combustion/ablation are stiff and uncertain.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Hardness results (275, 278, T1) set limits fast (P3); certified class-restricted functionals (frontier-xc-certified) are data- and compute-gated.

bottlenecks.name: Posing and formal trust of applied problems (the meta-bottleneck)
bottlenecks.description: To use AI mathematics, an engineering question must be stated precisely (assumptions, norms, regimes) and the answer trusted. The Oct 6 problem set was pure-math-skewed (16 PDE + 12 dynamics families of 372, 7.5%); Mathlib lacked Sobolev-space infrastructure as late as Sep 2026 (three groups built their own); formal applied benchmarks score ~35% (StochBench, Sep 2026).
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: <5% of today's effort, but the binding constraint for pathway P2 and for trusting P1 output (judgment)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-High and fast: agents now build missing library infrastructure cheaply (130k lines of topology in two weeks for ~$100, Urban 2026; Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium formalized in 10 days for $200, Ilin 2026). What stays human: reviewing definitions and statements (frontier-applied-posing).

nodes.title: Engineering math posed as precise problems
nodes.description: Engineers and AI agents translate engineering questions (a stability margin, an error bound, whether a sensor layout determines a material property) into precise mathematical statements with explicit assumptions, ideally Lean-stated, and pool them in open problem banks like the ~4,000 problems OpenAI posed for pure mathematics.
nodes.status_oct2026: No applied problem bank exists at that scale. The Oct 6 problem set was pure-math-skewed: 16 PDE and 12 dynamics families of 372; formalized 3 of 16 and 2 of 12. First applied formal benchmarks: CAM-Bench (May 2026, 1,000 Lean targets in optimization, numerical linear algebra, numerical analysis; many textbook concepts missing from Mathlib) and StochBench (Sep 2026, 450 stochastic-process problems; best agent 34.9%). Ilin (Mar 2026) formalized a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium result in 10 days for ~$200 with agents and zero human-written code; the failures were 'hypothesis creep' and 'definition-alignment bugs', which are posing errors, not proving errors.
nodes.why: For most applied problems the hard step is the statement, not the proof: which norm, which regime, which idealization. The catalog shows capability on hard PDE (362 Vlasov-Maxwell, the forced Navier-Stokes blowup), so the scarcity of applied results reflects what was posed. Under S2 models pose candidate statements from engineering context and agents build missing library pieces (Urban 2026: 130k lines of topology in two weeks for ~$100), so a 1,000+ problem applied bank is plausible by 2027. Human review of definitions remains essential (Ilin). This node gates frontier-xc-certified and frontier-math-unbinds and, outside this domain, every P2 verification chain.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Much of applied mathematics' value lies in modeling judgment that does not reduce to theorem statements; engineers do not think in theorems; export control (ITAR/EAR) and proprietary concerns will keep the most valuable space problems out of open banks, so posing stays artisanal inside each program.
nodes.signpost: NASA, ESA, DARPA or AIAA publishes a formally stated applied open-problem bank (500+ problems), or a lab releases 50+ PDE/numerics/UQ/control families in one release.

nodes.title: Euler blowup in open space, proven
nodes.description: A rigorous, likely computer-assisted, proof that the 3D incompressible Euler equations on R^3 with no boundary form a finite-time singularity from smooth, finite-energy data. It is the inviscid, unforced stepping stone to the Navier-Stokes question.
nodes.status_oct2026: Proven with a boundary by Chen-Hou (computer-assisted, 2022-23); Chen-Hou posted clarification notes in Jul and Aug 2026 answering a 2025 critique, so such proofs take years to settle. Low-regularity C^{1,alpha} blowup without boundary is known (Elgindi 2021, general; Chen May 2026). Smooth data on R^3: numerical evidence only. DeepMind's 'Discovery of unstable singularities' (Sep 2025) reached near double-precision profiles for the boundary case. Ganeshram-Duruisseaux-Anandkumar (Sep 2026) report a candidate self-similar R^3 profile and a stability framework; the finite set of explicit estimates is still missing. Forced Euler blowup was announced machine-checked by Alpoge-Buckmaster (Sep 2026). Not in the openai/math catalog.
nodes.why: All ingredients exist: an AI-found candidate profile, a stability framework, and computer-assisted estimate machinery. What remains is a large finite set of verified inequalities, which agentic proof plus interval arithmetic does well. Difficulty is at the level that fell on Oct 6 (judgment: 0 doublings beyond). Acceptance is the slow part: the bar is a Lean or independently re-run proof, given the Chen-Hou history. It unlocks frontier-ns-unforced and the MHD blowup question, since ideal MHD with zero field is Euler.
nodes.strongest_case_small: No engineering effect. Euler is inviscid, and any singularity would sit far below the molecular mean free path in a real fluid. Its value is as a credibility signal and a stepping stone.
nodes.signpost: A Lean- or interval-verified proof of smooth R^3 Euler blowup, with an independent re-run (Hexagon, Comparator or a second group).

nodes.title: Navier-Stokes Millennium problem settled
nodes.description: Resolution of the actual Clay statements (A)/(B) for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: global smoothness, or finite-time blowup from smooth data on R^3 or the torus.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open. OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim covers only the forced statements (C)/(D) (Lean, T3). A self-published replay (Sep 17, 2026) reports the Lean certificate builds with no sorry; this is not a Comparator run with a statement audit, so the tier is unchanged. Lei-Ren (Sep 28) wrote an expository reconstruction of the profile construction and call it 'a major advance'. Petrillo-Glimm (Sep 20) proposed the 'positive defect problem' as the target for a programmatic unforced search. Family 376 (T1) embeds universal computation in forced flows, Tao's proposed route to blowup.
nodes.why: One rung beyond what fell. Removing the forcing means the singularity must sustain itself against viscosity, likely via an unstable self-similar profile stabilized by a computer-assisted argument, or a Tao-style computing flow. Judgment: 1-2 difficulty doublings past the Oct 2026 level. Under S2 (a doubling every 6-9 months) the gap closes around 2029, and under S3 around 2028. Either answer acts only through P5. Years match the propulsion domain's prop-ns-clay-unforced.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Zero engineering effect. CFD codes regularize, any blowup would sit below molecular scales, and a regularity proof confirms what every code assumes. The public reception ('AI solved fluid dynamics') may exceed the technical effect; the paper should address this head-on.
nodes.signpost: A lab claims unforced blowup or regularity with a Lean proof and the Clay Institute responds; or no credible claim by end-2029, which favors S1.

nodes.title: Turbulence laws proven
nodes.description: Theorems that 3D Navier-Stokes with natural forcing (smooth, generic or white-in-time) dissipates energy at a rate independent of viscosity (the 'zeroth law') and obeys Kolmogorov-type inertial-range scaling, in a well-posed statistical framework.
nodes.status_oct2026: Onsager's conjecture is proven for Euler (Isett 2018; intermittent version Novack-Vicol 2023). Anomalous dissipation for forced Navier-Stokes is known only for constructed forcings (Brue-De Lellis 2023, general), now shown stable under geometric perturbation (C. Li, May 2026). Anomalous diffusion of passive scalars is proven (Armstrong-Vicol 2025), and the Kolmogorov 4/5 law holds conditionally for stochastic forcing (Bedrossian et al. 2019, general). The zeroth law for generic forcing and any intermittency correction remain open. No catalog family.
nodes.why: This is the theory engineering actually wants, because closures need statistics, not trajectories. It is harder than NS regularity in one respect: the right statements must be invented, so posing is part of the problem (judgment: 2-4 doublings plus posing). Chain: zeroth law and scaling, then a rigorous LES convergence theory (prop-les-convergence-theory), then closures with error bounds for canonical flows, then (data-gated) engineering closures (prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Kolmogorov scaling has been built into turbulence models since 1941, so a proof changes no RANS or LES practice. The costly engineering errors come from wall-bounded separation, transition, compressibility and chemistry, where DNS and experiment data bind, not theorems.
nodes.signpost: A proof of the zeroth law for Navier-Stokes on the torus with a fixed smooth or white-in-time forcing; or a lab release with a turbulence-theory family.

nodes.title: Boltzmann and Landau equations proven well-behaved
nodes.description: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness for the space-inhomogeneous Boltzmann and Landau equations with physical interactions (including Coulomb and very soft potentials), far from equilibrium. These are the kinetic equations behind rarefied reentry, DSMC and collisional plasmas.
nodes.status_oct2026: The space-homogeneous cases are done: Landau with Coulomb potential does not blow up (Guillen-Silvestre, Acta Math. 2025), and homogeneous Boltzmann with very soft potentials follows from monotone Fisher information (Imbert-Silvestre-Villani 2024). Inhomogeneous: regularity is known conditional on hydrodynamic bounds (Imbert-Silvestre program; Fernandez-Real-Ros-Oton-Weidner 2025), and a new continuation criterion rules out Euler-type blowup lifting into kinetics (Golding-Henderson-Silvestre, May 2026). The catalog claims 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation, T1) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases over its lifespan, with fluctuations, T1); 362 (relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) shows problems of this kind now fall.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (analog evidence: 362 at T3; 363/364 at T1, conditional)
nodes.why: Comparable in difficulty to 362, which was claimed in the Sep-Oct run, and the human program is close: conditional regularity reduces it to hydrodynamic bounds, and there is a new continuation criterion. Under S2 a lab that poses it settles it within a release cycle. Effect: P5 confidence for DSMC and kinetic codes, plus quantitative moment and decay bounds that feed solver error control (hyper-kinetic-solver-certification, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics).
nodes.strongest_case_small: DSMC and kinetic codes have matched wind-tunnel and flight data for decades. Any inhomogeneous blowup would occur far from reentry conditions. The binding errors in rarefied aerothermodynamics are gas-surface interaction and chemistry data.
nodes.signpost: A proof (human or AI) of global regularity for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, or a lab kinetic-theory family covering it.

nodes.title: Where fluid and kinetic models are not unique
nodes.description: A systematic set of nonuniqueness and ill-posedness results, with matching uniqueness criteria, for the Euler, Navier-Stokes, Boltzmann and MHD models engineers simulate. It marks which regimes need an extra selection principle (entropy condition, vanishing-viscosity limit, finer physics).
nodes.status_oct2026: Convex integration gives nonuniqueness of weak Euler and NS solutions (general), including for compressible Euler with Riemann data (Chiodaroli-De Lellis-Kreml 2015, general), and sharp forced nonuniqueness for SQG (ARMA, Oct 2026). Ill-posedness in supercritical Sobolev spaces (Duke, Aug 2026). Catalog: 363 Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation (T1); 376 universal computation in forced NS (T1); the Sep 8 forced NS blowup (T3).
nodes.why: Negative results act fastest (analyst position d). A nonuniqueness theorem for a regime tells V&V teams that solver-to-solver disagreement there may come from the equation rather than the code, and tells modelers where to add a selection principle. Convex-integration constructions are long, technical and constructive, which suits agents. Feeds frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd and hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The constructions use wild, low-regularity data (velocity below Holder 1/3) with no physical counterpart, and numerical dissipation already acts as a selection principle. Practitioners have lived with Scheffer-Shnirelman nonuniqueness since the 1990s without changing practice.
nodes.signpost: A nonuniqueness result for compressible NS or Boltzmann with physically reasonable data (bounded entropy, shock-tube-like), cited by a CFD V&V or DSMC group.

nodes.title: Landau damping proven for realistic plasmas
nodes.description: Nonlinear Landau damping (collisionless relaxation of plasma waves) proven beyond the idealized setting: Sobolev data, whole space, magnetized plasmas, weak collisions and full electromagnetic (Vlasov-Maxwell) fields, with explicit rates.
nodes.status_oct2026: Mouhot-Villani (2011, torus, Gevrey) is now Lean-formalized (Bedrossian, Sep 2026). Unconfined 3D near Poisson equilibrium (Nguyen-Wei-Zhang 2024-25); unconfined 2D (Ionescu-Nguyen, Sep 2026); screened two-species with large data (Mar 2026); weak-collision Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck (Luo 2024); Sobolev echo counterexamples (Bedrossian 2016, general). Magnetized and full Vlasov-Maxwell long-time behavior are open. Catalog 362 (T3) supplies global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, a prerequisite for long-time questions.
nodes.why: An active human program is closing in, and the difficulty is catalog-level. Formalization has started (Bedrossian), so kinetic theory is now formalizable despite the 3-of-16 PDE formalization rate. Downstream, quantitative damping rates and echo thresholds justify the linear dispersion relations used in electric-propulsion and space-weather wave models and inform kinetic closures (plasma-kinetic-closures). Overlaps the plasma domain's plasma-landau-longtime.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Plasma physics has used Landau damping since 1946 and confirmed it experimentally. Proofs give rates in small-perturbation regimes where linear theory already works, and Hall-thruster anomalous transport is turbulence, not damping.
nodes.signpost: A proof of nonlinear Landau damping for a magnetized Vlasov-Poisson or Vlasov-Maxwell system in Sobolev regularity.

nodes.title: Which plasma fluid models are well-posed
nodes.description: A map of well-posedness, singularity formation and ill-posedness for ideal, resistive, Hall and electron MHD in 3D, the models used for space weather, magnetic nozzles and fusion-propulsion concepts. A stretch goal is rigorous bounds on magnetic reconnection rates.
nodes.status_oct2026: Local well-posedness is classical. 3D global regularity is open and inherits Euler's difficulty: ideal MHD with zero field is Euler, so a smooth R^3 Euler blowup gives ideal MHD blowup directly. Hall-MHD is ill-posed near some steady states (Jeong-Oh 2022, general); reduced electron-MHD models form singularities (Dai 2025); ideal MHD below the classical threshold (Giardi, Sep 2026). Fast reconnection lacks rigorous theory. No catalog family.
nodes.why: Ill-posedness matters in practice: codes that include Hall terms need regularization, and a full map tells space-weather and nozzle modelers which models give results that converge under refinement (P3). Blowup results follow from Euler techniques, while reconnection-rate bounds are harder (judgment: 1-2 doublings). Weak feed to plasma-eruption-onset-theory and plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Space-weather forecast skill is limited by solar boundary data (magnetograms) and coronal physics, not well-posedness. Operational solar-wind codes carry known numerical diffusion that already regularizes.
nodes.signpost: A proof of finite-time blowup or of ill-posedness for 3D Hall-MHD or ideal MHD from smooth data, or a rigorous resistive reconnection-rate bound.

nodes.title: Long-term orbital stability with real constants
nodes.description: Quantitative KAM, Nekhoroshev and Arnold-diffusion theorems for realistic n-body parameters: rigorous lower bounds on stability times and upper bounds on diffusion rates for the solar system, resonant asteroid and cislunar orbits, and long-lived constellation dynamics.
nodes.status_oct2026: Arnold diffusion is proven in the planetary spatial 4-body problem (Clarke-Fejoz-Guardia, Publ. IHES 2024), and a degenerate mechanism in the restricted 3-body problem (Guardia-Paradela-Seara, Ann. ENS, Dec 2025). KAM for planetary systems is known only for tiny masses (general). Solar-system instability is known numerically (Laskar: ~1% chance of Mercury destabilizing in 5 Gyr, general). The catalog touches only model maps: 146 Sinai positive entropy of the standard map (T1), 347 strong Arnold fixed-point counterexamples (T3), 343 sharp symplectic ball packing (T1). It has no n-body results.
nodes.premise_tier: T1/T3 (model maps only; n-body target unproven)
nodes.why: KAM and Nekhoroshev constants are notoriously tiny. Theorems with realistic constants need high-order normal forms with interval arithmetic, exactly the long, careful work agents scale (judgment: 1-2 doublings plus heavy computation). Finite-horizon (years to decades) transport bounds for cislunar orbits are easier and expert-scarce; they belong to astro-nbody-transport-proofs and astro-stability-atlas, which this node strengthens.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Missions use numerical propagation with margins and station-keeping, so billion-year stability theorems change nothing operational. The effect lands in astronomy and planetary science, not in flown systems.
nodes.signpost: A computer-assisted proof of explicit stability-time or diffusion-rate bounds for a realistic Sun-Jupiter-Saturn or Earth-Moon resonance configuration.

nodes.title: Derivatives of chaotic averages
nodes.description: Theorems that long-time averages of chaotic systems (turbulent flows, plasma turbulence, the thermosphere) depend differentiably on design parameters, with computable bounds and convergent algorithms. This is the mathematics that would let adjoint and gradient optimization work on unsteady turbulent systems.
nodes.status_oct2026: Linear response is proven for uniformly hyperbolic systems (Ruelle, general) but fails or is unproven for most realistic, non-hyperbolic dynamics. Shadowing-based sensitivity methods work heuristically at high cost (general). Rigorous enclosures of Lyapunov exponents exist for stochastic flows (2024). Catalog: 146 Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map (T1), a famous non-hyperbolic chaos problem, suggests the capability has reached this terrain.
nodes.why: Adjoint design is routine for steady flows but breaks for unsteady chaotic flows, because pathwise sensitivities grow like exp(lambda*t). Combustors, nozzles and thrusters are therefore designed by sampling, at roughly one simulation per parameter direction. A theorem saying when averaged sensitivities exist, with an algorithm, would turn chaotic-flow design into gradient optimization with thousands of parameters (frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design). A negative answer would also help (P3), since it ends a research line. This is an under-appreciated node: less famous than Navier-Stokes, far more consequential for design.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization with a few hundred simulations already handles modest parameter counts. Realistic flows may lack linear response in the needed regimes, and most design value comes from validated physics models, not gradients.
nodes.signpost: A proof of linear response with a convergent sensitivity algorithm for a non-uniformly hyperbolic flow class (a Lorenz-type flow or a Galerkin-truncated Navier-Stokes system).

nodes.title: Proven limits for scheduling and network planning
nodes.description: Hardness-of-approximation ceilings for the combinatorial problems behind constellation tasking, ground-station siting, routing and network partitioning become verified theorems rather than beliefs, so planning tools and vendor claims are judged against known limits.
nodes.status_oct2026: Catalog: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3), which makes Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut (0.878) and 2-approximate vertex cover optimal; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e, about 1.736 (T3); 117 uniform sparsest cut hardness (T3); 104 quasipolynomial mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games (T3); 124 polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines (T1); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1); 111 matroid prophet inequalities (T1). No outside Comparator run reported as of Oct 7, 2026; repo has a single initial commit.
nodes.why: Ceilings take effect within months (P3), once they are independently checked. Most were already believed, so the change is from belief to theorem: research spending moves from better general approximation algorithms to instance structure, exact MIP on small instances and learned heuristics. Volumes are large (Starlink performed 144,000+ collision-avoidance maneuvers in six months, per 33FG), but these are operational problems where structure dominates. This node bounds frontier-scalable-global-certificates.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Worst-case hardness says little about structured operational instances, and satellite scheduling already solves well in practice (branch-and-cut-and-price, EJOR 2025). These ceilings were assumed for 20 years.
nodes.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on families 102, 125 and 117 (Hexagon or Buzzard's group).

nodes.title: How hard neural networks are to verify
nodes.description: A complete complexity map for verifying the properties of neural networks used in perception and control (robustness, reachability, Lipschitz bounds), including which architectures or training regimes make verification tractable.
nodes.status_oct2026: ReLU network verification is NP-complete (Katz et al. 2017, general). Sep 2025: deciding positivity of an l-layer ReLU network is W[l-1]-hard in input dimension; approximating the maximum or the Lipschitz constant is NP-hard; naive n^((l-1)d) enumeration is essentially optimal under ETH (Froese et al.). Tractable classes are partly characterized. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) supplies hardness machinery; nothing is NN-specific.
nodes.why: Ceilings tell assurance architects that exact verification of large perception networks will not scale (exponential in input dimension under ETH). That pushes flight designs toward runtime assurance (simplex wrappers; verif-runtime-assurance) and verifiable-by-construction controllers. Positive results on tractable classes feed verif-nn-verification-scale. Complexity theory is the area where AI math is already strongest (40 TCS families, 20 with Lean).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already know NN verification is hard and already use runtime monitors. The real blocker is specification: there is no formal statement of what 'detect the docking port' means.
nodes.signpost: A tractability theorem for a practically used architecture class (for example Lipschitz-constrained CNNs at flight scale), or fixed-depth hardness of approximate robustness certification.

nodes.title: Capacity limits of laser and quantum links settled
nodes.description: Proofs of the ultimate data rates of the optical and quantum channels used for deep-space laser links and satellite QKD (bosonic thermal-noise channels, amplitude damping), turning conditional capacity formulas into theorems.
nodes.status_oct2026: Catalog: 273 entropy photon-number inequality (T1), which makes capacity formulas for bosonic thermal and broadcast channels unconditional; 276 classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping (T3); 272 entanglement without secret key (T1); 266 exactly three MUBs in dimension six (T1). Quantum capacities with superadditivity remain open (general).
nodes.why: Link budgets for optical deep-space and inter-satellite links quote capacity bounds. These become unconditional (P5 confidence), and QKD security proofs gain exact limits. Bands are one step down from the P5 default because the key premise (273) is T1. Under S2, verification bandwidth rises and 273 likely reaches T4 by 2027.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Engineers already used the conjectured formulas, and real links run far below capacity because of pointing, atmosphere, detector efficiency and coding. Effect on hardware: nil.
nodes.signpost: Independent verification of 273 (Lean or expert reconstruction), and citation in CCSDS optical-link standards rationale.

nodes.title: P vs NP resolved
nodes.description: Resolution of P vs NP, or of the barrier problems around it (superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits).
nodes.status_oct2026: Open. The relativization, natural-proofs and algebrization barriers explain why known techniques fail (general). No catalog family.
nodes.why: Harder than anything that fell. The barriers mean a proof needs genuinely new techniques, not more effort (judgment: many doublings beyond Oct 2026, possibly not bridgeable by scaling). Downstream it is nil either way: P != NP is already assumed by all cryptography and planning, and a practical P = NP algorithm is considered extremely unlikely.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Even a proof of P != NP changes no engineering practice. It is included to show the ceiling of the exponential premise.
nodes.signpost: Superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits, or a method that provably evades the natural-proofs barrier.

nodes.title: AI finds a crack in post-quantum crypto
nodes.description: An AI-produced cryptanalytic result that materially lowers the security of a standardized post-quantum scheme (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) or of the structured lattice problems underneath (Module-LWE), forcing parameter or algorithm changes.
nodes.status_oct2026: NIST standardized FIPS 203/204/205 in Aug 2024 (general); a 2024 claimed quantum lattice algorithm was withdrawn after a bug was found (general). Aug 2026: an autonomous agent workflow broke eight published academic constructions at their stated parameters (Ring-LWR commitment, middle-product encryption, a lattice e-voting protocol, and others), none of them standardized (Olejnik-Naskrecki). Catalog: 279 exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set (theory only) and 138 Subset Sum in 2^0.49n (T1) do not touch deployed cryptography.
nodes.why: Module-LWE has survived about 20 years of study, but the capability is strongest at constructive, adversarial search, as the Aug 2026 breaks of academic schemes show (analyst position f). The space angle: satellites fly cryptography in hardware for 5-15 years, so even a parameter-level weakening mid-life forces rekeying or algorithm changes that many buses cannot make. Crypto agility is the hedge regardless of the probability.
nodes.strongest_case_small: AI breaks so far hit lightly vetted academic schemes. Standardized parameters carry tens of bits of margin, and hybrid classical-plus-PQC deployment means a partial break is not exploitable.
nodes.signpost: Any AI-produced improvement to lattice-sieving or reduction asymptotics, or a concrete attack on a standardized or round-4 NIST scheme.

nodes.title: Optimal control with proven guarantees
nodes.description: Existence, regularity and dimension-robust approximation theorems for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and reachability equations with state constraints, plus certified a posteriori error bounds for neural and tensor solvers, so guidance and collision-avoidance policies come with proofs.
nodes.status_oct2026: Viscosity-solution theory is mature (general). State-constrained and hybrid HJB regularity is partial. Grid solvers scale exponentially: 100 points per axis in 6 dimensions is 10^12 nodes. Neural and tensor solvers mostly lack guarantees, though verifiable error bounds for PINN Lyapunov/HJB solutions appeared (Liu, Mar 2026), along with policy iteration under control constraints (Kundu-Kunisch, Sep 2026). Catalog: 104 quasipolynomial stochastic/parity games (T3) is the discrete analogue; 139 log-concave sampling (T3).
nodes.why: GNC teams mostly need bespoke guarantees, such as a reachable-set bound for one vehicle or a stability certificate for one controller. These are expert-scarce rather than open and easier than catalog problems. With research-grade applied math public (S2: 2027) they become on-demand, and they can be checked formally once infra-mathlib-applied matures. Downstream: astro-scp-guarantees, verif-closed-loop-guarantees, hyper-certified-edl-guidance, astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Flight GNC already uses convex formulations (lossless convexification) that carry guarantees; the residual risk is model mismatch, not math. For general HJB classes the curse of dimensionality is a lower bound, so guarantees will cover structured cases only.
nodes.signpost: A certified a posteriori error bound for a neural HJB solver in 6+ state dimensions, used in a published collision-avoidance or EDL guidance study.

nodes.title: Certified global optima for nonconvex design
nodes.description: Moment-SOS, branch-and-bound and MIP methods that certify a trajectory, layout or design is globally optimal, or within a proven gap, at engineering scale, using sparsity, symmetry and convergence-rate theory.
nodes.status_oct2026: Lasserre hierarchies converge, with finite convergence generically (general). Rate theory is advancing (Schlosser et al. 2025; Tran-Toh 2026; Henrion-Safey El Din, Sep 2026), and sparse tightness is characterized (Nie-Qu-Tang 2025). Scale is the limit: a degree-4 moment relaxation in n = 100 variables has a moment matrix of side C(102,2) = 5,151. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) implies SDP-based ratios are worst-case optimal for many problems.
nodes.why: Certificates for specific instances are not ruled out by worst-case hardness. Exploiting problem structure (sparsity, symmetry, term sparsity) is expert-scarce, technique-heavy work that compounds under S2. Downstream: astro-global-optimality-certificates, verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates, and design-space closure for prop-ai-engine-design-loop. The value is assurance and an end to search; performance gains are typically a few percent of delta-v or mass in complex designs (general).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Engineers rarely need global optimality, only feasible-and-good. Local optimizers with multistart already find near-optimal designs, so certification buys assurance, not performance.
nodes.signpost: A certified global optimum (proven gap under 1%) for a published multi-gravity-assist or constellation-design benchmark with 100+ decision variables.

nodes.title: Guaranteed error bars for smooth-regime simulations
nodes.description: A posteriori estimators and computer-assisted methods that give guaranteed, not asymptotic, error bounds for nonlinear PDE solutions in smooth regimes: heat conduction, structures, laminar and steady flows, electrostatics. This is the bulk of spacecraft analysis outside turbulence.
nodes.status_oct2026: Guaranteed a posteriori bounds are mature for linear elliptic problems (general). Validated integrators exist for semilinear parabolic PDEs (van den Berg-Breden-Sheombarsing 2024; simplified Jan 2026), and computer-assisted PDE proofs are routine for special problems (Ayala-Lessard 2026). NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024) requires credibility assessment but accepts estimated numerical error. No catalog family.
nodes.why: The methods exist in pieces. Applying them per problem (deriving the estimator and the constants for a given nonlinear operator) is expert-scarce, and AI does it on demand once applied math is public. Guaranteed bounds can replace three-level grid-convergence studies, which cost roughly 3-10x a single solve (general). Downstream: hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics, prop-cfd-auto-vv, materials-multiscale-certified, and frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Discretization error is rarely the dominant error in space analysis; model-form and input uncertainty dominate. Guaranteed bounds are often 10-100x loose, too loose to drive decisions.
nodes.signpost: A NASA or commercial thermal-structural code ships guaranteed a posteriori bounds for a nonlinear analysis, or NASA-STD-7009 guidance credits them.

nodes.title: Error bars for turbulent and shocked flows
nodes.description: Rigorous statistical error bounds for simulations of chaotic, turbulent and shock-laden flows (combustors, plumes, reentry wakes), bounding errors in averaged quantities rather than in individual trajectories.
nodes.status_oct2026: No such theory exists. Pathwise error grows exponentially in chaotic flows, and nonuniqueness results (convex integration; 363 and 376, T1) show the limit equations may not select a unique answer without extra principles. Practice relies on grid studies and validation data; turbulence, transition and separation are the leading CFD gap (CFD Vision 2030, general).
nodes.why: This is the hardest applied node, and possibly impossible in pointwise form. What is achievable: bounds on statistics under ergodicity assumptions, with the selection principle stated explicitly and model-form error estimated from data. It chains four upstream nodes, two of them genuinely open, so even S3 stays Low. If it lands, it would make CFD credibility in prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure and prop-cfd-auto-vv a computed quantity rather than expert judgment.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Even if achieved, closure (model-form) error dominates and is set by data, so the bound would be correct but large. Engineers would still calibrate against tests.
nodes.signpost: A rigorous convergence-of-statistics theorem for LES of forced turbulence on the torus, with explicit rates.

nodes.title: Stiff chemistry solvers with certified error
nodes.description: Error theory and verified implementations for stiff ODE/DAE integration of large reaction networks (combustion, ablation, plasma chemistry, batteries), including error bounds for reduced mechanisms that hold for non-dissipative chemistry.
nodes.status_oct2026: Classical stiff theory (A- and B-stability, B-convergence) assumes one-sided Lipschitz or dissipative structure that combustion chemistry lacks (general). Order reduction is understood for linear problems (2025). Verified ODE integration exists in Isabelle (IsaVODEs 2024; 'Numerical Methods in Isabelle', Jan 2026), not yet at reaction-network scale. Catalog: 149 permanence of weakly reversible reaction networks (T1) gives structural boundedness for an important class of chemistry models.
nodes.why: Mostly expert-scarce: AI can derive mechanism-specific error bounds and produce reduced mechanisms with a proven bound on ignition delay or species error. Reducing a ~50-species mechanism to ~15 typically cuts chemistry cost several-fold in reacting CFD (general). Downstream: prop-stiff-chemistry, hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-battery-life-qual.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Rate-constant uncertainty, often a factor of 2-10, dwarfs integration error, and CVODE-class solvers with tolerance control are already adequate. Certification addresses the smaller error.
nodes.signpost: A certified reduced mechanism, with a proven bound on ignition delay, adopted in a rocket-engine CFD code.

nodes.title: Certified rare-event probabilities
nodes.description: Methods with provable, non-asymptotic error bounds for very small failure probabilities in high-dimensional, non-Gaussian models: 1e-4 collision probabilities, 1e-6 structural failure, margins. Covers importance sampling with certified variance, large-deviation bounds and certified surrogate-based UQ.
nodes.status_oct2026: Practice uses multilevel Monte Carlo, subset simulation and importance sampling with asymptotic or sample-based guarantees (general). Conjunction assessment at scale relies on Gaussian approximations (Starlink: 144,000+ maneuvers in six months, per 33FG), and space-weather drag uncertainty feeds directly into Pc (Parker et al. 2024). Catalog: 139 subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling (T3) and 140 memory-sample lower bounds for regression (T3) give ceilings. 360 Villani convexity/regular OT (T3) and 374 sharp 1/3 stability of OT maps (T1) bound transport-map filters (weak link).
nodes.why: Certified estimators are mostly expert-scarce, so on-demand AI unlocks them fast. Data binds the answer, though: no estimator beats the information in the data. Demonstrating 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ln(0.1)/ln(0.99) = 230 tests unless a validated physics model carries the extrapolation. Structural example: raising a monocoque shell buckling knockdown factor from 0.65 to 0.8 through certified imperfection statistics cuts buckling-critical wall thickness by sqrt(0.65/0.8) = 0.90, about 10% of that mass. Downstream: astro-nongaussian-uq-certified, hyper-certified-margin-uq, materials-allowables-stats-framework, prop-life-twin.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Engineering decisions use conservative margins anyway, and a certified estimator of a mis-specified model gives a precise wrong answer. Model-form error is not a mathematical object.
nodes.signpost: A conjunction-assessment provider publishes certified, non-asymptotic Pc bounds for non-Gaussian cases at catalog scale, or NASA-STD-7009 guidance cites certified rare-event estimators.

nodes.title: Radiation transport with error bounds
nodes.description: Deterministic and Monte Carlo radiation-transport methods (crew and electronics shielding, radiative heating during entry, neutronics for nuclear propulsion) with proven convergence and error bounds in the full 6+1-dimensional phase space, including asymptotic-preserving and low-rank solvers.
nodes.status_oct2026: Space-radiation codes predicted Artemis I absorbed dose blind, from Earth to Mars, accurately across ISS, Orion, BioSentinel and Mars-surface measurements (Slaba et al. 2025). Dominant remaining uncertainties are nuclear cross sections and biological response, not transport mathematics (general). Low-rank and asymptotic-preserving schemes lack general error guarantees (general). No catalog family.
nodes.why: The mathematical gap is real but expert-scarce rather than deep, so it falls once applied math is on demand. The effect is lower V&V cost and certified low-rank solvers fast enough for design loops, not better dose accuracy. Downstream: hyper-radiation-kinetics (radiative heating), prop-ntp-fuel-model (neutronics), materials-see-system-models (single-event effects).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Dose prediction is already validated to engineering accuracy; nuclear data and radiobiology dominate the error budget.
nodes.signpost: A certified low-rank transport solver used in a design analysis (an NTP core or crew-shielding trade).

nodes.title: How much sensor data is enough
nodes.description: Quantitative stability estimates, not just uniqueness, for the inverse problems behind structural health monitoring, heat-shield inspection, gravimetry and tomography: how measurement noise and sensor placement bound the damage or material properties that can be recovered.
nodes.status_oct2026: Catalog: 372 global uniqueness for smooth isotropic Lame moduli from boundary data (T1); 365 joint metric-plus-connection recovery from one boundary patch, with conductivity nonuniqueness (T3); 366 planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity (T1); 368 3D Ball-Evans approximation (T1); 369 hot spots conjecture for planar simply connected domains (T1). Uniqueness typically comes with only logarithmic stability for Calderon-type problems (general), which is why practice relies on regularized inversion calibrated by test.
nodes.why: Uniqueness says the data suffice in principle; stability constants for a given sensor layout say how many sensors and what noise level are needed. That is bespoke, expert-scarce work AI does on demand. Bands are one step down because most premises are T1. Downstream: hyper-tps-inverse-nde, materials-am-digital-twin-qual.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Logarithmic stability means practical recovery depends on priors and regularization, not the theorem. NDE practice is calibrated by coupons and rarely changes sensor counts because of theory.
nodes.signpost: A sensor-placement design derived from a stability estimate, used in a flight structural-health-monitoring system or a TPS inspection protocol.

nodes.title: Density functionals with proven error bounds
nodes.description: Exchange-correlation functionals, learned or constructed, with provable or rigorously certified error bounds on defined chemical classes relevant to space (propellants, ablators, high-temperature alloys, electrolytes), within the limits set by hardness results.
nodes.status_oct2026: The exact functional exists, but computing it is QMA-hard (Schuch-Verstraete 2009, general). The catalog tightens the limits: 275 QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy (T1) and 278 failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability (T1); also 263 ionization conjectures (T3). Learned functionals now beat hybrids at semi-local cost: Skala reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on GMTKN55 (Luise et al., Jun 2025) and was implemented in CP2K in Aug-Sep 2026. None carries an error certificate.
nodes.why: The hardness results (P3, acting now) say no universal efficient functional exists, so the path is class-restricted functionals certified against high-accuracy wavefunction references. Defining the class is a posing problem; generating CCSD(T)/QMC reference data is a compute-and-data problem. Downstream: materials-learned-functionals, hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-energetics-design. Overlaps materials-dft-limits, which owns the hardness side.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Learned functionals already improve accuracy empirically, and materials programs validate by experiment anyway, so a certificate adds little. Reference-data cost binds, not mathematics.
nodes.signpost: A functional published with a proven or statistically certified error bound on a defined chemical class and adopted by a propulsion or materials group.

nodes.title: Gradient design of turbulent and chaotic systems
nodes.description: Design tools that compute reliable sensitivities of time-averaged quantities in unsteady turbulent or plasma flows (combustor stability margins, nozzle heat loads, thruster erosion), enabling gradient optimization over thousands of parameters instead of sampling.
nodes.status_oct2026: Steady adjoint design is routine in aerospace (general). For chaotic unsteady flows conventional adjoints diverge, and shadowing methods are costly and heuristic (general).
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (rests on an unproven theory node)
nodes.why: If frontier-chaos-linear-response lands (S2: 2029), turning it into a tool is method design plus validation of designed hardware against tests, which is the binding physical gate. S3's autonomous labs compress validation, hence Medium. Downstream: prop-ai-engine-design-loop, prop-stability-design-tool, plasma-ep-predictive-design. The gain is design-space exploration at about the cost of two simulations per gradient instead of one per parameter.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization already handle tens of parameters well; most design value comes from validated physics models; and a theory result may come back negative.
nodes.signpost: A published gradient-based optimization of an LES combustor or Hall thruster with 1,000+ design parameters, validated by test.

nodes.title: Math expertise stops limiting space programs
nodes.description: The scarce resource in space-program analysis is no longer people who can do research-grade applied math. Stability proofs, error bounds, optimality certificates and well-posedness checks are requested from AI like compute, and schedules are set by tests, data and certification instead.
nodes.status_oct2026: Such work is expert-scarce today. Public models handle much routine analysis; research-grade capability is internal and unreleased.
nodes.why: Under S2 the cognitive clock runs years ahead of the physical one. Engineering math needs, mostly easier than the catalog, are met by about 2028-29, and the binding constraints become tests, data and qualification (analyst position g). Rough scale: if analysis and V&V take ~20-30% of development engineering hours (general) and AI halves the mathematical share, program-level savings are ~5-15%, unless test campaigns also shrink, and they compress far less. This is the domain's main point for readers: the exponential mostly accelerates what was never the long pole.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Organizations change slowly. Liability and certification require human sign-off, and much 'math' work is modeling judgment and data interpretation that stays with people.
nodes.signpost: A prime contractor or NASA center reports replacing a specialist analysis function (for example GNC stability analysis) with AI-produced, human-reviewed proofs on a flight program.

scenario_contrast: The frontier compresses along a difficulty ladder, measured from what fell on Oct 6, 2026 (UGC, quasi-RH, forced NS blowup = level D0). Expert-scarce applied problems (HJB guarantees, certified error bars in smooth regimes, rare-event estimators, stiff and transport error theory, inverse-problem stability) sit below D0: capability is not the constraint. Access, posing and formal trust are. Kinetic regularity, general Landau damping, Euler blowup on R^3 and the nonuniqueness map sit at about D0. Unforced Navier-Stokes, realistic-constant n-body stability and linear response for chaotic systems sit 1-3 doublings beyond. Turbulence laws sit 2-4 doublings beyond, plus posing. Certified turbulent CFD needs several open nodes at once, and P vs NP is beyond scaling (barriers). S1 (Plateau): the D0 problems fall 2028-29, applied nodes wait for public access and land 2029-30 (Medium), and everything past D0 except the MHD map slips past 2031; 10 of 26 nodes are >2031. S2 (Exponential, base case): with difficulty doubling every 6-9 months and public access in 2027, D0 problems fall in 2027, applied nodes in 2027-28 (mostly High), unforced NS and the chaos/n-body nodes in 2029, turbulence laws in 2030, and certified turbulent CFD in 2031 (Low). Only P vs NP stays beyond 2031. The median node arrives about 2 years earlier than in S1. S3 (Recursive) moves the hard cognitive nodes another ~1 year (unforced NS 2028, turbulence 2029) and lifts the experiment-gated tool node (gradient design of chaotic systems) to Medium through autonomous validation. P vs NP and a structural break of standardized lattice crypto stay Speculative or Low. Across all three, what binds is not proving but: (1) independent verification bandwidth (Chen-Hou's 2022-23 Euler proof was still drawing clarification notes in Jul-Aug 2026); (2) posing (the Oct release was 7.5% PDE/dynamics by family because that is what was asked); (3) applied formal infrastructure (three groups built their own Sobolev theory in Lean in 2026; StochBench best agent 34.9%); and (4) for anything touching physical closure, data. Shared upstream years assumed (matching the propulsion domain): cap-research-math-internal and cap-autoformalization 2026; cap-research-math-public S1 2028 / S2 2027 / S3 2027; cap-applied-math 2029 / 2027 / 2027; cap-physics-theory >2031 / 2028 / 2028; cap-design-optimization 2030 / 2028 / 2028; infra-verified-numerics 2030 / 2028 / 2028; infra-mathlib-applied 2030 / 2028 / 2027 (this domain's assumption); verif-independent-check 2027 in all three.
key_insights: The key question answered: for the applied problems space engineering actually needs, AI capability is not the binding constraint, since the Oct 2026 model already exceeds what most bespoke engineering math requires. The constraints bind in this order: (1) access (the model is unreleased); (2) posing (stating the engineering question precisely; the Oct release was 7.5% PDE/dynamics by family because that is what was posed); (3) formal trust (applied Mathlib coverage and verified numerics lag informal capability by roughly 2-3 years); (4) data, wherever physics closure is involved. Capability still binds only for the genuinely open frontier: unforced Navier-Stokes, turbulence laws, realistic-constant n-body stability, linear response of chaos, P vs NP.

Strongest evidence on posing vs capability: an agentic workflow formalized a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium result in 10 days for ~$200 with zero human-written code, and its failures were 'hypothesis creep' and 'definition-alignment bugs' (Ilin, Mar 2026). Proving was cheap; stating correctly was the work.

The Mathlib gap for PDE is real but closing fast. As late as Apr-Sep 2026, three separate groups built their own Sobolev-space infrastructure to formalize elliptic theory, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser and 2D Navier-Stokes Galerkin, and Bedrossian formalized Mouhot-Villani Landau damping (Sep 2026). Agents now build library infrastructure for ~$100 per textbook (Urban 2026), so under S2 the formal layer catches up around 2027-28. The human bottleneck that remains is reviewing statements.

Order of fall under S2: 2027, kinetic regularity (inhomogeneous Boltzmann/Landau), general Landau damping, Euler blowup on R^3, the nonuniqueness map, NN-verification complexity, verified approximation ceilings, plus on-demand HJB guarantees and rare-event estimators; 2028, MHD well-posedness, certified error bars for smooth regimes, certified stiff and transport solvers, inverse-problem stability, scalable global certificates; 2029, unforced Navier-Stokes, realistic n-body constants, linear response of chaos, certified density functionals; 2030, turbulence laws and gradient design of chaotic flows; 2031, certified turbulent CFD (Low); after 2031, P vs NP.

The famous frontier problems have near-zero engineering effect. Navier-Stokes either way, Euler/MHD blowup and billion-year solar-system stability act only through P5 (confidence). What changes engineering are negative results (nonuniqueness tells V&V where the equation, not the code, is at fault) and quantitative by-products (rates, constants, error bounds).

The most consequential unsolved math for space design is not Navier-Stokes but linear response of chaotic averages. It would make gradient-based design of unsteady combustors, nozzles and thrusters possible over thousands of parameters. Under S2 it lands around 2029 (Medium), with tools around 2030 (Low).

Certified error bars split cleanly. Smooth regimes (thermal, structures, laminar) are expert-scarce and land around 2028 under S2 (High). Turbulent and shocked flows may be impossible in pointwise form; nonuniqueness results say what can be certified is statistics plus an explicit selection principle, and model-form error stays data-bound (2031, Low).

Cheap math does not beat data. Demonstrating 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes 230 tests unless a validated physics model carries the extrapolation. Certified rare-event estimators and UQ become routine (High under S2) but move margins only where the models are validated.

Cryptography watch: AI agents broke eight published academic constructions in Aug 2026, while standardized PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) is intact. A structural break by 2031 is Low under S2/S3, but satellites carry hardware crypto for 5-15 years, so crypto agility is the hedge whatever the probability.

The exponential premise has an honest ceiling inside mathematics itself: verification bandwidth. Chen-Hou's computer-assisted Euler proof (2022-23) was still being clarified in Jul-Aug 2026, and no outside Comparator run on openai/math had been reported by Oct 7, 2026. Under S2, proofs arrive faster than the community can certify them unless verification is itself automated (verif-independent-check).
nil_effects: Unforced Navier-Stokes resolved either way: no CFD code, turbulence closure, engine or vehicle changes. Codes already regularize, and any singularity would sit below molecular scales.
Euler and ideal-MHD blowup proofs: no change to space-weather forecast skill, which is limited by solar boundary data (magnetograms) and coronal physics.
Billion-year solar-system stability theorems: no change to mission design, which uses numerical propagation over years with station-keeping margins.
Galactic speedups in the release (matrix-multiplication exponent, sub-n-log-n Fourier transform): no change to onboard compute, signal processing or orbital data centers.
P vs NP: nil either way in practice. P != NP is already assumed by all cryptography and planning software.
Radiation dose accuracy: already validated blind on Artemis I. The remaining error is nuclear cross sections and radiobiology, not transport mathematics.

Reliability demonstration: test counts for zero-failure demonstrations (230 tests for 0.99 at 90% confidence) do not shrink because of mathematics alone. Only validated physics models can stand in for tests.
Density functionals: hardness results (275, 278, conditional) mean no universal efficient functional, so materials programs still need experiments and expensive reference calculations.
Deployed cryptography: nothing in the release weakens RSA, elliptic-curve or standardized post-quantum schemes.
Physical clocks: launch cadence, test-stand time, qualification campaigns and certification timelines are untouched by any frontier theorem in any scenario.

signposts.event: First independent Comparator run plus statement audit on openai/math families (especially 102, 362) or on the Sep 8 forced Navier-Stokes proof, by Hexagon, Buzzard's group or another outside party
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves premises from T3 to T4 and raises the bands of frontier-approx-ceilings and frontier-optical-quantum-capacity. A failure would push every frontier node about a year later and reprice the 245 unformalized families.

signposts.event: A Lean- or interval-verified proof of smooth Euler blowup on R^3 (2027 under S2)
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the S2 pace on the PDE frontier and unlocks frontier-ns-unforced and the MHD blowup question. If nothing appears by end-2028, shift toward S1.

signposts.event: A lab claims unforced Navier-Stokes blowup or regularity (S2: about 2029; S3: about 2028)
signposts.what_it_changes: The clearest test of the exponential premise in this domain. Its engineering effect stays nil, and the paper should say so in advance.

signposts.event: A lab or public model produces 20+ applied-math families (PDE estimates, numerics with certified bounds, UQ, control) in one release
signposts.what_it_changes: Tests the posing hypothesis. If applied families appear as soon as they are posed, capability was never the constraint for applied math, and frontier-applied-posing plus the tier-2 nodes move up a year.

signposts.event: Mathlib merges Sobolev spaces, distributions and basic elliptic/parabolic theory, and applied formal benchmarks (CAM-Bench, StochBench) exceed 80% agent solve rates
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms infra-mathlib-applied on the S2 track (2028), opening P2 verification for numerics and control proofs.

signposts.event: Research-grade math model publicly available to outside teams (OpenAI or a rival) with pricing
signposts.what_it_changes: Turns on P1 for all tier-2 frontier nodes; the S1-to-S2 difference for applied nodes is mostly this date.

signposts.event: A proof of global regularity for the inhomogeneous Landau or Boltzmann equation
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms that the D0-level kinetic problems fall on schedule (2027 under S2) and firms up DSMC and kinetic-solver foundations.

signposts.event: Any AI-produced improvement to lattice-sieving or reduction asymptotics, or an attack on a standardized PQC scheme
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves frontier-lattice-crypto-watch from Low to urgent. Space programs with fixed hardware crypto would need agility retrofits.

signposts.event: NASA, ESA, DARPA or AIAA publishes a formally stated applied open-problem bank
signposts.what_it_changes: Directly relieves the posing constraint and pulls frontier-applied-posing to High under S1.
